notes: One NBBO bid/ask per RTH minute, taken at the minute BOUNDARY, for the five tradables. It exists to answer one question: the H=1 gain is concentrated in LLY, the name whose last-trade price flips hardest between the buyer's and the seller's side, and XOM, whose price barely flips, loses - which is the signature of bid-ask bounce rather than a real edge. A midpoint price cannot bounce, so the same test run on mid separates the two, and no bar field can substitute (vwap manufactures a positive lag-1 up to +0.25 by Working (1960), twenty times the effect being measured). Raw quotes are NOT stored: the cohort averages about 3.1 million NBBO updates per session, so the connector folds pages of raw quotes down to one row per minute in flight and only the row reaches disk. symbols are in PULL ORDER and each carries its own cursor: LLY and XOM are the decisive pair (all of the apparent signal, and none of it), so they complete before a request is spent on the other three. start is 2024-11-01, NOT the 2016 bar history: at the free tier's 200 requests per minute of 10,000 quotes each, the full 2022-05 walk-forward era would take about 23 hours for five names, and this 16-month window - roughly the last five fold validation windows plus the whole holdout tail to the cut - costs about five and a half hours and is enough to measure the one-minute autocorrelation to a standard error near 0.003 against an effect of -0.046. end is the study's hard data cut, EXCLUSIVE, declared where the fetch happens so a quote at or after it is never requested. Quotes are UNADJUSTED - Alpaca has no adjustment knob on this endpoint - so a row is on the as-traded scale of its own day, like the alpaca-sip bar tree and unlike alpaca-sip-split; no split falls inside this window for these five names, but a reader joining mid to split-adjusted bars outside it must rescale. budget_seconds bounds one job so a long backfill is a sequence of resumable pulls rather than one that loses everything when it is interrupted. It was 3000 and is now 570, because an interruption is not hypothetical here: the detached pull was killed mid-job when the shell that launched it was terminated, discarding seven minutes of staged work that had not reached a commit. A cursor only advances on a completed session and a job only commits at its end, so the budget IS the exposure - 570 seconds puts a commit inside every ten-minute window and costs a few seconds of setup per job. Backfill only: there is no live mode on a source with a data cut behind us. Secrets are environment-variable names; the material never enters this file or any hash.
